feature.label: General SEM Simultaneous Two-Way PLS Moderation Full-Model Case Bootstrap

claim.supported_scope: Opt-in Experimental Labs gamma-only inference for one or more jointly estimated two-operand interaction_v2 terms in a newly created single-group recursive general_sem_v1 PLS composite model, using deterministic indexed full-model case resampling, two-stage construction, strong hierarchy, two-sided Type-7 percentile intervals, sample standard errors, null-centered plus-one probabilities, and an exact 90 percent usable-replicate gate.
claim.estimand: One stable scientific rescaled gamma per compiled interaction effect relation: the replicate joint-stage coefficient on the sample-standardized product divided by that replicate product's sample standard deviation after complete shared stage-one refitting and score-vector sign alignment.
assumptions: The schema-6 project is newly created with general_sem_v1 authority and the structural graph is direct-only and acyclic.
Every interaction has exactly two stable operands, two-stage construction, strong hierarchy, an exact focal relation, and all required lower-order paths.
Raw continuous data are unweighted, single-group, processed with the frozen listwise-complete scoring boundary, and contain no authored missing-value markers or transformation lineage.
Every target and receipt remains bound to the same recipe, model, dataset, compiled plan, stage-one projection, seed, and exact capability identity.
exclusions: Bootstrap inference for standardized-product beta, ordinary joint-stage coefficients, fixed minus-one/zero/plus-one slopes, and plot points is excluded; those values remain point-only even though every replicate recomputes and validates them.
BCa, studentized, basic, one-sided, residual, parametric, Bayesian, weighted, clustered, and stratified resampling are excluded.

Three-way interactions, moderated mediation, directed structural chains, requested indirect or total effects, authored probe policies, higher-order constructs, groups, weights, feedback, and legacy-project migration are excluded.
warnings: The independent evidence is a bounded observed-score smoke that never calls production code; it does not establish indicator-level PLS score recovery, nominal coverage, null calibration, random-stream parity, SmartPLS numerical parity, native/package qualification, or release qualification.

Connected engine, native, canonical, and persistence paths do not by themselves establish semantic export equality, packaged Windows acceptance, performance/soak qualification, or promotion readiness.
A statistically nonzero interaction coefficient does not by itself establish a causal moderation mechanism.

equations.expression: p_i = z(x_i) z(w_i); z(p_i) = (p_i - mean(p)) / sd_sample(p)
eta_y = sum_r beta_r eta_r + sum_j beta_product_j z(p_j) + epsilon_y; gamma_j = beta_product_j / sd_sample(p_j)
CI = [Type7(alpha/2), Type7(1-alpha/2)]; SE = sqrt(sum((gamma_b-mean)^2)/(U-1)); p = (count(|gamma_b-gamma_0| >= |gamma_0|)+1)/(U+1); U >= max(2,ceil(0.9B))

references.citation: Henseler and Chin (2010), A Comparison of Approaches for the Analysis of Interaction Effects Between Latent Variables Using Partial Least Squares Path Modeling
SmartPLS public moderation and bootstrapping documentation, used only as a documented terminology, workflow, and observable-output benchmark

Validation-only independent observed-score same-focal and different-focal joint case-bootstrap reference for scientific gamma, Type-7, B-minus-one standard error, plus-one probability, and the exact usable gate

simulations.design: Two deterministic 80-row observed-score proxy systems with two simultaneous interactions each: one same-focal equation and one different-focal equation. Each system uses 199 independently indexed case resamples; every replicate restandardizes score proxies, resolves deterministic artificial sign ambiguity before products, rebuilds and rescales products, refits the complete joint OLS equation, and validates all ordinary, interaction, gamma, fixed-probe, and normal-equation values. Only four scientific gamma targets are summarized as inference, and production QuickPLS code is never imported, called, or compared.
simulations.seed_policy: Frozen SHA-256 scenario/replicate/draw indexed case positions with forward-versus-reverse evaluation replay; this independent stream deliberately makes no production-stream identity claim.
simulations.acceptance_rule: Every frozen check passes; all 398 observed-score refits per replay are usable, four and only four scientific gamma targets receive inference, replay error and joint normal-equation error are at most 1e-10, every interaction product scale varies across indexed replicates, deterministic sign corrections occur before products, Type-7/B-minus-one/plus-one microcases are exact within 1e-10, and the gate accepts 18 of 20 but rejects 17 of 20. This is an engine smoke, not a full PLS or release-qualification simulation.

simulations.design: A fully independent indicator-level PLS implementation over same-focal and different-focal simultaneous interactions across loading, path, moderator correlation, sample size, reliability, unequal scale, nonnormality, missingness, collinearity, sign ambiguity, and controlled stage-one and joint-stage failure axes.
simulations.seed_policy: Pending frozen scenario-indexed data and independent case-resampling streams with every failed fit retained in the requested denominator.
simulations.acceptance_rule: Pending independent full-PLS qualification; the observed-score reference does not claim that this gate has run.

simulations.design: Null, positive, negative, unequal-scale, correlated-predictor, nonnormal, boundary-sample, rank-deficient, sign-indeterminate, and controlled-failure full PLS populations for simultaneous same-focal and different-focal interactions.
simulations.seed_policy: Pending frozen indexed scenarios with failed replicates retained and exact seed/worker replay.
simulations.acceptance_rule: Pending qualification-scale calibration and independent review; no nominal error-rate claim is made by this manifest.

boundaries.case: A case sample has insufficient observations, a constant indicator or score, rank deficiency, an isolated construct, stage-one nonconvergence, indeterminate sign, a constant product, joint-stage rank deficiency, or another numerical failure.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Retain one typed failure at the exact replicate index; publish no result if usable replicates are fewer than max(2, ceil(0.9B)).

boundaries.case: The request contains a directed chain, mediation estimand, authored probe, higher-order construct, three-way interaction, unsupported product construction/hierarchy, group, weight, transformed input, non-listwise missing policy, non-percentile interval, or non-two-sided tail.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Preserve the authored model and return a corrective blocked capability decision without silently simplifying it or falling back to point-only execution.

boundaries.case: Eligible declarations are consistently reordered, case evaluation scheduling changes, or permitted positive affine observed-input transformations are applied under the frozen preprocessing and score-orientation contract.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Mapped target identities, gamma summaries, failure ledger, and scientific receipt remain equivalent within tolerance.

boundaries.case: The same valid resident recipe is repeated with identical seed and different supported worker counts.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Gamma summaries, ordered failures, usable-index digest, and all scientific receipts are identical after normalizing operational worker metadata.

boundaries.case: A model, dataset, compiled plan, stage-one digest, target identity, interaction metadata, point estimate, product scale, inference value, usable count, failure row, method version, or receipt digest is altered.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Strict canonical and schema-6 validation rejects the attachment or reopened project and exposes no partial bootstrap result.

tamper_tests.expected_behavior: Reject a result whose exact supplemental moderation-bootstrap cell differs from its recipe, point primary cell, compiled plan, or receipt.
Reject a result relabeled with another point, bootstrap, stream, quantile, standard-error, probability, failure, sign-alignment, product-scale, or gamma-target version.
Reject a result whose resident dataset fingerprint or complete-case frame identity differs.
Reject a changed archive member, compiled-plan digest, gamma-target identity-set digest, usable-index digest, or canonical attachment digest.
Reject duplicate keys, unknown fields, nonfinite values, unordered targets or failures, incoherent counts, non-gamma inference rows, or contradictory full-model execution flags.
Never attach this capability to an ordinary or historical project without newly created schema-6 general_sem_v1 authority.

persistence.legacy_policy: This exact capability applies only to newly created schema-6 general_sem_v1 projects; no legacy migration or upgrade-copy route is provided.

applicability_blockers: Unsupported interaction, topology, estimator, data, group, or inference predicate
Stale recipe, model, dataset, compiled plan, point primary cell, or target identity
Failed point fit or fewer than max(2, ceil(0.9B)) usable replicates
result_surfaces: Bootstrap mean, bias, B-minus-one standard error, Type-7 interval, and plus-one probability
Requested/usable counts and ordered typed failures
Method, target, compiled-plan, dataset, and resampling provenance
Point-only joint coefficients, fixed probes, and plots from the primary point artifact
native.gui_cli_parity_rule: For identical resident recipe, model, data, compiled plan, seed, workers, point artifact, and supplemental capability identity, every product surface must read the same canonical result. The same-app native execution and schema-6 append/reopen paths are connected, but independent cross-surface, semantic-export, packaged, and release qualification remain pending.
accessibility_rules: Every gamma estimate, interval, probability, usable/failure count, typed failure, and unavailable reason is available without relying on color, canvas position, or pointer-only interaction.
Point-only slopes and plots remain explicitly distinguished from gamma inference in visible and programmatic labels.
